title: Oncall handoff notes - Isaac Morris (Feb 28 - Mar 3 2026)
content:
Shift summary (Feb 28 18:00 UTC -> Mar 3 06:00 UTC)

Quick notes: busy weekend but mostly noisy alerts. Two recurring issues: 1) host disk pressure on pool-prod-03 causing degraded batching throughput; 2) intermittent 503s surfaced by canary route (route: /v1/generate-canary). Both have mitigations in place; follow-ups listed below.

Active incidents:
- INF-3421 (disk-pressure, pool-prod-03) — LOW->MED after manual cleanup and temporary eviction. Root cause: logrotate misconfiguration + stale profiler dumps.
  - Timeline: 2026-03-01 01:14 UTC: first disk pressure alert (node-exporter: node_filesystem_avail_bytes < 5%); 01:20 UTC: batch queue latency spike -> autoscaler started evicting low-priority pods; 01:33 UTC: manual cleanup (rm -rf /var/tmp/profiler-dumps/*) + restarted vector on node.
  - Mitigation applied: cleaned dumps, increased logrotate frequency to daily for /var/log/runtime-profiles, temporarily added a larger ephemeral volume to pool-prod-03 (attached by infra team).
  - Next steps: create a CronJob to purge profiler dumps older than 3 days (INF-3505), fix logrotate config (PR #1234), and add disk usage alert -> ticket INF-3506.

- INF-3490 (canary 503s on /v1/generate-canary) — intermittent; currently degraded but stable.
  - Symptoms: user-facing canary traffic saw ~1-2% 503s for ~90 minutes on Mar 2 22:10-23:45 UTC. No large CPU/mem spikes.
  - Action Taken: rolled canary route back to model variant v2-rc1 -> immediate reduction in 503 rate. Enabled extra logging at runtime (trace-level for router) and collected KV cache stats.
  - Hypothesis: an uncommon code path in v2-rc2 causes a race when handling empty-tool calls + streaming; leads to uncaught exception in router that returns 503.
  - Follow-ups: create a reproducible unit test for empty-tool-call path, coordinate with serving-runtime team (assign to Ravi), and hold v2-rc2 rollout until patch merged (INF-3512).

Ops status and checkpoints:
- Pager queues: cleared. No on-call escalations to SEV.
- Queues to watch next 12h: batching-latency, canary-503-rate, kv-cache-hit-rate.
- Monthly maintenance: snapshot window scheduled Mar 7 02:00 UTC (reminder to tell infra: ensure Dedicated pools have low traffic).

Important commands & quick runbook (temp procedures)
- Check disk pressure on node:
  - kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep pool-prod-03
  - ssh node -> df -h /var/lib/kubelet
  - kubectl describe node <node> | grep -A5 "Non-terminated Pods"

- Cleanup old profiler dumps (temp manual):
  - ssh node
  - sudo du -sh /var/tmp/profiler-dumps/* | sort -h
  - sudo rm -rf /var/tmp/profiler-dumps/older-than-7d*  # temp, will be replaced by cronjob

- Restart vector (log forwarder) on node (if logs not shipping):
  - sudo systemctl restart vector
  - sudo journalctl -u vector -f --no-pager

- Rolling back canary route to previous model variant (fast rollback):
  - api call: POST /internal/routes/rollback {"route":"/v1/generate-canary"}
  - OR use console: Routes -> canary -> Rollback to v2-rc1
  - Confirm: watch 503-rate in metrics for 10min

Open action items (owner in parentheses):
- INF-3505: CronJob to purge profiler dumps older than 3d (Isaac) — draft CronJob exists in gist, needs review from infra.
- INF-3506: Add disk-usage alert threshold to alerting, include ephemeral vol usage (Leah) — PR submitted for alert rules but needs tuning.
- INF-3512: Block v2-rc2 rollout until router fix + unit test (Ravi) — assigned, in progress.
- INF-3515: Postmortem template (short) for canary 503s (Isaac + Ravi) — start draft, due Mar 6.

Notes to next on-call (things I would watch closely):
- When you see disk pressure on pool-prod-03, don't just restart pods. Check for large files under /var/tmp/profiler-dumps and /var/log/runtime-profiles first. We had an instance where a restart moved logs around and made eviction worse (because the kubelet re-wrote a lot of checkpoints).
- For canary 503s: try rollback first if the rate > 1% sustained for 15 minutes. If rollback doesn't reduce errors, flip canary to zero traffic and open an incident.

Workarounds and temporary configs applied this shift (recorded for rollback):
- Attached ephemeral volume to pool-prod-03: vol-ephemeral-2026-03-01 (created via infra). Remember to detach when cleaned (ticket INF-3522).
- Increased logrotate frequency for /var/log/runtime-profiles to daily (temp) via adhoc script on pool-prod-03. This is noisy; revert after CronJob rollout.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Why did profiler dumps accumulate? Need to check whether a recent profiler agent change toggled dump-on-failure default. Check PRs merged around Feb 10-20 (potential suspect).
- Confirm whether CI job that runs model cleanup is honoring TTL for old artifacts. I saw many model-cache folders with >30d age.

Useful links / references:
- Confluence runbook (serving): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/12345/Model+Serving+Runbook
- Pager history/logs: https://pager.redwood.internal/archives/2026-02 (internal)
- Related Jira: INF-3421, INF-3490, INF-3505, INF-3512
- Slack: #sre-oncall (use @oncall to page team)

Misc notes / scratchpad:
- Quick hypothesis for 503: router throws on nil stream object if the client sends EOF immediately after headers (race). Need to add defensive nil-checks.
- Temp script used: https://gist.github.com/isaacm/abcdef (contains cleanup command; ephemeral)

Handoff checklist for next shift (please ACK in Slack):
- [ ] Review INF tickets listed above and add yourself as watcher if you own one.
- [ ] Verify pool-prod-03 disk usage is < 60% (df -h) before leaving.
- [ ] Check canary 503-rate (Grafana panel: Canaries -> /v1/generate-canary)
- [ ] If any sevs start, follow normal incident template and notify oncall@redwood.com

If anything urgent, ping me (Isaac) on Slack or call. I set my phone to DND but will wake for SEV.

-- Isaac
